# Uniform check soundness of the alternating replacement codes

## 1. Claim and exact imports

Work over F2. Let `C_k = (C_k^0 --d_k^0--> C_k^1 --d_k^1--> C_k^2)` be the alternating RX/RZ family of Balasubramanian–Davydova–Lin, **arXiv:2605.10943v1**, sections 3.2.2–3.2.6, starting with a constant planar surface-code seed. Use a fixed odd subdivision parameter `ell >= 3`, `t=(ell-1)/2`, and the natural cancellation squares. Every nonzero X/Z check overlap in this seed has size two. This property is preserved by the replacements below.

The source-proved inputs used here are:

* The total-complex definition, the cellular stars `Y_x,Y_q,Y_z`, and restriction connecting maps in equations (59)–(73).
* `Y_x` is connected and `H^1(Y_x;F2)=0`; `Y_q` is connected. These are the local cellular facts in the proof of Lemma 3.8, equations (76)–(80). They are hypotheses about the published replacement class, not consequences inferred from a passing finite computation.
* RZ is the dual replacement of section 3.2.5; reversing cochain degree exchanges X and Z and transposes the RX maps.
* Uniform Tanner vertex degree `D=7` and edge/face incidence `E=4` (Lemma 3.14), fixed `ell` independent of level, exponential size in level, and existence of a bounded-density, finite-range R3 embedding (Theorem 1.2 and section 3.2.7).

The contribution proved here is an explicit degree-one local retraction with two disjoint coordinate projections, its transpose, and the resulting **uniform polynomial check-soundness**. We then apply an established stability theorem. We do **not** equate this with perturbed finite-temperature storage, efficient initialization, physical interactions, or a practical error threshold.

Write `S_X(C)=im d^0` and `S_Z(C)=im (d^1)^T`. Let `f_k^X(M)` be the largest, over X stabilizers of weight at most M, of the minimum number of supplied X generators whose product is that stabilizer; define `f_k^Z` similarly. Set `f(0)=0`.

There are finite constants A,K,p, depending on ell and the degree bounds but **not on k**, such that

`f_{2k}^X(M), f_{2k}^Z(M) <= K M^p` for every integer `M>=1`.

Consequently the complete CSS stabilizer group has check-soundness function `2 K M^p`, uniformly in k, with no small-weight cutoff required for this combinatorial statement.

and the full `compile_complex.py` / `check_retraction.py` code. Matched the
load-bearing definitions to the primary memory source2605.10943v1,
Sections3.2.2--3.2.7 and the actual five-qubit seed of Section3.3. Read the
relevant definitions, Lemma24 and formal AppendixC theorem of
[Yin--Lucas2411.01002v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.01002v2).

**Verdict:** the uniform polynomial check-soundness theorem and its qualified
zero-temperature spectral-stability consequence are mathematically accepted.
No substantive error or required change was found. This is a whole analytic
and implementation inspection, not an independent numerical replay of the
finite matrices. No new replacement level, trajectory or thermal experiment
was run. The actual contribution is the filling/retraction bridge; the
stability theorem itself is an established operation.

degree bases, doubled boundary cylinders, restrictions and dual replacement

all depths of THIS family. They are not inferred from finite ranks or
silently generalized to arbitrary overlap pairings.

**Disjoint projections.** Each selected Q point is used by only its own old
q. Each selected X edge lies on one x--q ray, is used only by q, and is in

# Independent all-level admission check

29 October 2026. This supplements the whole review of A's
`RETRACTION_PROOF.md`; it is not another finite-level computation. The
governing physical family is the main alternating replacement family of
[arXiv:2605.10943v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10943v1), Sections3.2--3.3,
with its actual five-qubit planar seed and its natural cancellation squares.

The reviewer verifies the following invariant package. It is stronger than
checking a few ranks, but does not extend admission to arbitrary LDPC Tanner
square complexes with arbitrary higher-overlap pairings.

1. Every qubit is incident to at least one check of each color.
2. Every nonzero X/Z check intersection has exactly two qubits, with its
   unique natural cancellation square.
3. For each check v of either color, the graph L_v=partial X_v is connected.

The main seed has X supports {0,1,2},{2,3,4} and Z supports
{0,2,3},{1,2,4}, up to labels. Its four intersections have size2. For
example L_X0 is the path 0--Z0--2--Z1--1; the other three check links have
the same path form. All qubits have both colors. Thus all three conditions
hold in the literal seed used by the exact consumer and in the primary
five-qubit surface seed.

## Cone and suspension structure

For an old X check x, every z vertex of L_x has degree2, by condition2.
Its two q neighbors are the shared qubits of x,z. Add a virtual diagonal
x--z inside their unique square; its two triangles show that X_x is a PL
cone on L_x. This is just a subdivision of the specified square, not a new
Hamiltonian check or a change of cancellation pairing.

The doubled Y_x is therefore a PL suspension of L_x, with the intervening
cylinder included. Since L_x is connected, has an edge and has no isolated
vertices, the link of EVERY vertex of a square subdivision of Y_x is
connected. At an apex the link is L_x. Away from the apices the local model
is an interval times a nonempty star, or the corresponding half-model;
punctured neighborhoods are connected. Subdivision preserves this fact.
In particular H1(Y_x;F2)=0, equivalently reduced H0(L_x)=0, as used in
the primary Lemma3.8. The local X-face pool consequently fills every tree
fundamental cycle used in A's degree-one homotopy.
